intel.t: Main message: she runs as the Alaskan against a Washington insider, saying Sullivan arrived with $3M and now has $8M, while calling herself pro-development and a champion of the oil industry.

Biggest vulnerability as opponents frame it: Sullivan calls her a Lower 48 liberal, 16 times at one forum, and attacks her post-Congress lobbying income and a reported staff mistreatment story she calls gossip.
Strongest coalition: Alaska grassroots donors. She was the first Alaska Native woman elected to Congress and has more Alaska donors than Sullivan.
Primary showing: she led the August 18 top four primary, 49.5 percent to 41.4 percent in the August 28 count.
Notable recent event: a $17M third quarter and a final debate on October 16 that turned to personal attacks over wealth, lobbying and staff.
Air war: AdImpact shows over $9M reserved by each side for the final three weeks, Republicans slightly ahead.

bottom: Peltola is the best funded challenger in this batch and one of the poorest candidates. Her principal committee took in $18.55 million through July 29, 2026, $16.26 million of it from individuals, per Legis1 on August 19, 2026, https://legis1.com/news/sullivan-peltola-campaign-donors-follow-the-money-1. The campaign then reported $17 million for July through September, relayed by Congress.net on October 13, 2026, https://congress.net/?p=9621. She reports assets as low as $47,000.
Three interests combine money with a decision she would touch:

**National Democratic leadership.** Senate Majority PAC reserved $10 million in May and more than $12 million by October. Most of her PAC money came from Democratic leadership PACs. The decision is the Senate majority.
**Small donors.** Nearly $3.5 million of her first quarter came in unitemized gifts, mostly through ActBlue, and she has more Alaska donors than Sullivan.

intel.t: Main message: Alaska resource development and a Republican Senate, casting Peltola as a Lower 48 liberal who would let Democrats block ANWR.

Biggest vulnerability as opponents frame it: personal enrichment in office, with Peltola saying his wealth went from $3M to $8M; Newsweek relays an $8.4M Quiver estimate. He answers by attacking her lobbying.
Second vulnerability: a thin home base. Only about $135,000 of his first quarter money came from Alaskans, and he trailed Peltola in the primary 41.4 percent to 49.5 percent.
Strongest asset: cash and outside air cover, with $7.30M cash against her $4.64M and $17M from the Senate Leadership Fund.
Notable recent event: a second Dan Sullivan is on the ballot after the Alaska Supreme Court ruled on June 29; the incumbent is listed as the registered Republican incumbent.
Final debate October 16 turned on wealth, lobbying and staff treatment.

bottom: Sullivan has been outraised by Mary Peltola every quarter but kept a cash lead and a heavier outside air war. His principal committee, Alaskans For Dan Sullivan, FEC C00570994, reported $9.14 million in receipts and $7.30 million in cash, per Legis1 on August 19, 2026, https://legis1.com/news/sullivan-peltola-campaign-donors-follow-the-money-1. The Senate Leadership Fund put $17 million behind him, per Congress.net on October 13, 2026, https://congress.net/?p=9621.
Four interests combine money with a decision he controls or shapes:
**Senate Republican leadership.** The Senate Leadership Fund, the NRSC and the RNC ground game. The decision is the majority.
**Pro-Israel donors.** AIPAC passed about $250,000 in earmarked gifts to him in the first quarter of 2026 alone. The decision is Israel aid and the Iran war.

D.t: Mary Peltola leads by 5.1 in the forecast and wins 83% of simulations. The cushion is about 14,791 votes; a one point swing is about 1,450 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +1.7 and D +11.9. A normal polling error decides it.
The polls page average is D +3.4. Your best recent poll is New York Times/Siena at D +6.3; your worst is Trafalgar Group (R) at R +0.8. 9 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Anchorage Municipality, a projected net 15,739 votes; Juneau City and Borough, a projected net 7,148 votes; Bethel Census Area, a projected net 3,049 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.

The large counties within 12 points: Fairbanks North Star Borough, R +2.1, 12.6% of the vote; Ketchikan Gateway Borough, R +2.5, 1.9% of the vote; Kodiak Island Borough, D +10.7, 1.7% of the vote; North Slope Borough, D +8.9, 0.8% of the vote.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 77% of voters, 44 to 49, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.85 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 69% of voters, 50 to 44, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.45 points; Midsize counties, 68% of voters, 48 to 47, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.40 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Mary Peltola: Immigration voters 24 to 68, Incomes $125K and up 40 to 53, Men 44 to 50. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.

Sabato's Crystal Ball moved the Alaska Senate race from Toss-up to Lean Democratic, a projected Democratic pickup.
Interviewed Democrat Mary Peltola about her challenge to Sen. Dan Sullivan.
Discussed Mary Peltola's Alaska focused campaign messaging alongside Talarico controversies.
Listed Alaska as a toss up Senate race where Democrats lead by 3, and warned Democrats to trust no one as GOP has beaten polls in Trump states.
Said he worries about Alaska for Dan Sullivan.
Called Alaska a coin flip, noting Mary Peltola led the first round.
His polling average showed Mary Peltola slightly ahead of Dan Sullivan, 48.1% to 46.6%.
On Anderson Cooper 360 he said polling in the Alaska Senate race is tilting toward Democrats.
Predicted in Reason that Republicans will lose the Alaska Senate seat.
Grilled Attorney General Todd Blanche on State of the Union over the Justice Department suit to block certification of Alaska's Senate race if Dan Sullivan loses, asking what crime is alleged.
Called the Justice Department's lawsuit over the Alaska Senate race a dirty trick.
